To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a reference map of proteins from white lupin roots was generated by proteomic analysis, and that the combined EST and protein data sets will facilitate the understanding and utilization of white lupin for phytoremeditation and other agronomic traits.

we generated an expressed sequence tag (EST) database for developing white lupin roots and identified candidate genes and root proteins for antimicrobial defense, (heavy) metal transport and translocation, and phosphate acquisition.
the ESTs and proteins identified in this study are involved in the response of white lupin to phosphate starvation, heavy metal uptake and antimicrobial defence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of cluster roots and their function in metal uptake, and with the identification of antimicrobial compounds produced by white lupin.
the identification of genes and proteins that are differentially expressed in white lupin roots under different conditions, and their potential use in breeding for improved agronomic traits.
the identification of candidate genes and proteins that may play important roles in the development of white lupin root system and its response to biotic/abiotic stress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the white lupin root ESTs and proteins will provide the basis for further research to elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of white lupin roots and its responses to environmental stresses.

the white lupin root transcriptome and proteome have been characterized for the first time, providing a solid foundation for further studies of the mechanisms involved in the adaptation and defense of white lupin roots to biotic and/or abiotic stresses.

the white lupin ESTs and proteomic data provide a valuable resource for the identification of genes and proteins involved not only in metal uptake and accumulation but also in other processes of agronomic significance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined EST and protein data sets provide a valuable resource for the understanding of white-lupin's response to abiotic and biotic stresses.
the ESTs and proteins obtained in this study provide a valuable resource for further studies on the mechanisms of white lupin responses to biotic and/or abiotic stresses.

this study has generated a valuable resource of ESTs and proteins from white lupin root tissues and has provided a foundation for further research on the molecular mechanisms of root development and root stress responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
proteomics can be used for the analysis of root proteins and the identification of proteins that are involved in metal uptake and transport.

the combined EST and protein data sets will facilitate the understanding and manipulation of white lupin root development, and its responses to biotic and biotic stresses, as well as its potential utility for phytomining and phytoremediating (heavy) metals.
white lupin is a model plant that has a lot to teach us about the mechanisms of plant adaptation to environmental stresses and the development of specialized root structures.
